'''Pacawara''' ('''Pacahuara''') is a nearly extinct dialect of the [[Panoan languages|Panoan]] [[Chácobo language]]. The [[Pacahuara]] have been located to northwest of Magdalena, [[Beni Department|Beni]], [[Bolivia]]<ref>{{cite book|last1=Moseley |first1=Christopher |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=p-7ON7Rvx_AC&pg=PT227|title=Encyclopedia of the World's Endangered Languages |date=10 March 2008 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-135-79640-2 }}</ref> and to Nueva Esperanza municipality, of [[Federico Román Province]] in [[Pando Department|Pando]].<ref>{{Cite news | title = CIDOB pedirá 54 mil hectáreas de tierras para el pueblo Pacahuara | work = Erbol Comunicaciones | accessdate = 2011-05-28 | date = 2011-05-05 | url = http://www.erbol.com.bo/noticia.php?identificador=2147483944186 }}</ref> Pacahuara is recognized as an official language of Bolivia by the 2009 [[Constitution of Bolivia|Bolivian Constitution]].<ref>First Part, Title I, Chapter One, Article 5: ''Model of State'', [http://www.presidencia.gob.bo/download/constitucion.pdf Nueva Constitución Política del Estado] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090521023641/http://www.presidencia.gob.bo/download/constitucion.pdf |date=2009-05-21 }}, p. 3.</ref>

A recent report shows how their culture is on the brink of disappearing.<ref>{{Cite news |title=The last of Bolivia's Pacahuara tribe |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/av/world-latin-america-21168061 |access-date=2025-03-06 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref>
